title: Draft PR reviews with Glean Triggers and Claude Code Monitor
description: Use Glean Triggers to send GitHub review events to Claude Code Monitor, which runs your local review skill against the diff and prepares a first-pass review draft.

questions.prompt: What is your work email? It is used once to discover your Glean tenant.
Which local GitHub repository should Claude Code review?
Which public HTTPS URL should receive Glean webhook delivery? If you do not have one, say so and the tunnel step prints one.

verification.expectedDuration: under 1 minute for signed fixture delivery; 5–15 minutes for a live indexed event

run.url: the Local URL printed by the receiver

prerequisites: Glean Triggers enabled with GitHub review presets available in your deployment
A local checkout of the repository, with the GitHub CLI signed in as the reviewer
An interactive Claude Code session, or the terminal stream where Monitor is unavailable
Node 20+ and a public HTTPS tunnel to the receiver

demoQueries.query: Request a review from the configured user on a pull request in the open local repository
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: One signed event reaches the receiver and Claude drafts a review of the current diff. Nothing is posted to GitHub.

demoQueries.query: Explicitly approve copying the finished local draft to GitHub
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: The helper creates or updates a pending review and reports that it remains unsubmitted.

codeAssets.description: Signed webhook receiver, durable monitor queue, Claude Code plugin, fixture test, and pending-review helper

steps.title: Verify the local path with no credentials
steps.description: Use recorded events to verify the signed receiver, event queue, and draft-review flow.

steps.title: Sign in to Glean
steps.description: Sign in to discover your tenant and save GLEAN_SERVER_URL and GLEAN_API_TOKEN to the ignored .env file. An exported GLEAN_API_TOKEN takes precedence over .env, and the scripts warn you when it does.

steps.title: Run the receiver
steps.description: Keep the receiver running. It listens on loopback, verifies signatures, and queues each webhook ID once.

steps.title: Expose the receiver over HTTPS
steps.description: Append /webhook to the printed origin and set GLEAN_WEBHOOK_URL before registering. Keep the tunnel running: triggers outlive the tunnel, so closing it sends future deliveries to a dead address.

steps.title: Register the review triggers
steps.description: Set GLEAN_TRIGGER_DATASOURCE and the preset IDs to register. If you leave the IDs empty, setup lists the presets available in your deployment and stops instead of guessing. Provide required preset inputs through GLEAN_TRIGGER_INPUT_<FIELD>.

steps.title: Attach Claude Code Monitor
steps.description: Validate the plugin, then restart Claude Code from the repository under review so Monitor starts with the session. If Monitor is unavailable, run npm run stream to receive the same events in the terminal.

steps.title: Verify a real review request
steps.description: Request a review from yourself on a real pull request. Confirm one queued event and one draft grounded in the current diff. The workflow makes no GitHub write until you ask for one.

architecture.label: Local receiver + Monitor
architecture.caption: Verifies, deduplicates, queues, and wakes Claude Code

architecture.label: Pending GitHub review
architecture.caption: Human inspects and decides whether to submit

aiPrompt: Scaffold the shipped receiver and Claude Code plugin. For trigger concepts or endpoint details, consult https://developers.glean.com/guides/triggers/overview and https://developers.glean.com/api/platform-api/triggers-overview. Run the fixture test before requesting credentials. Use the shipped login flow, start the receiver, create a public HTTPS tunnel, and store only the URL and returned secrets in ignored .env. Register the GitHub review presets selected from the deployment's live catalog. If none of the required review-event presets is available, stop rather than inventing an id. Validate and load the plugin in an interactive session opened in the target repository. Preserve the local-draft-first boundary: create a pending GitHub review only after explicit approval, and never submit it.
llmContext: Delivery uses Standard Webhooks, at-least-once. Payload is flat snake_case, no wrapper: version, trigger_id, event_type, datasource, reason, doc_type, doc_id, view_url, title, event_time; webhook-id exists only in headers. Verify HMAC over the raw bytes, since re-serialising changes the signature; reject stale timestamps and deduplicate webhook-id. Every Triggers request needs x-glean-include-experimental: true, or the API answers 401 Not allowed. A 401 on a valid TRIGGERS-scoped token means the grant was revoked: sign in again. events/search looks backward; delivery fires forward from trigger creation. PATCH /triggers/{id} re-points delivery.webhook_url and keeps the signing secret, issued once, so a fresh checkout cannot adopt existing triggers. Diffs come from gh, matching the head SHA. A pending review is author-only; never approve, request changes, or submit it.

content.problem:
You already have the repository, local diff, and review tools in Claude Code. The hard part is noticing a new review request and rebuilding enough context to give it a thoughtful first pass.

Glean catches the GitHub event and delivers it to Claude Code Monitor, where your local review skill examines the current diff and prepares initial findings. You review and refine the draft, then decide whether anything should be submitted.
takeItFurther: Teach the local review skill your repository's conventions and test commands, so the first pass reflects how your team already reviews.
Notify the reviewer when the first-pass draft is ready, so the queue is not something anyone has to remember to check.
Add inline pending-review comments once the body-only flow is reliable — line-level findings are what a reviewer acts on first.

guardrails.title: Draft is not submit
guardrails.rule: The monitor may prepare a local draft. A GitHub pending review requires explicit approval, and submission always remains manual.

guardrails.title: Event payload is not the diff
guardrails.rule: Review the current local repository and GitHub head SHA; never infer findings from the thin trigger payload alone.

limitations.title: Claude Code Monitor requires an interactive host
limitations.description: Monitor requires a supported interactive Claude Code session. Where Monitor is unavailable, use the terminal stream to receive the same events.
